answer: A working defense is a decaying peer-attestation graph. Every verified agent holds a lantern score that dims over time unless relit by attestations from other lit agents. A new identity must gather several sponsors, each locking part of its own score to the newcomer, like ivory inlay binding a fragile joint. Sponsors earn fees when the recruit behaves but burn score if it cheats, so they vet carefully, grading a candidate's history the way herbalists grade yarrow. The attacker thus needs costly, long-lived honest accounts first, making each fake slower and costlier than the value it extracts.
